CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (audit caught this): provision_type was miscoded general_cruelty despite this row's own notes and the parent US-FED jurisdiction row both explicitly stating no general federal cruelty offence exists - recoded to killing, matching the dictionary's definition (unlawful/cruel killing of a protected/covered animal) and this statute's actual focus on specific lethal/injurious methods. Covers purposely crushing, burning, drowning, suffocating, impaling, or otherwise inflicting serious bodily injury on a 'living non-human mammal, bird, reptile, or amphibian' - fish and invertebrates explicitly absent from the definition. Originally enacted 1999 targeting only 'crush videos' (depictions); the PACT Act 2019 expanded it to criminalize the underlying CONDUCT itself - the single most significant federal expansion in the 2015-2026 window. The commonly-cited '$250,000' fine figure likely derives from the GENERAL federal felony fine schedule (18 U.S.C. S3571) rather than being S48-specific - left blank here as unconfirmed rather than asserted. NO GENERAL FEDERAL CRUELTY OFFENCE EXISTS beyond this narrow, commerce-tied provision - general cruelty/neglect/abandonment/killing is exclusively STATE law in the US (see ALDF's 50-state rankings, referenced in PRD SS7, for that layer). NEW NOTE 2026-09-21 (volunteer Jennifer Ferrarese, reading 18 U.S.C. S48 directly, flagged two real gaps): (1) The conduct offense in S48(a)(1) is jurisdictionally narrow - it only reaches crushing that is 'in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce' or occurs 'within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States' (verified against the current codified text, law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/48). A purely private, non-commercial act with no interstate-commerce nexus and no federal-enclave/maritime connection could fall outside this specific federal statute's reach - but this is NOT the same as the underlying act being lawful: S48(e) expressly states the section does not preempt state law, and every US state's own cruelty statute (the ALDF 50-state layer referenced above) would independently cover the same intentional killing/torment regardless of any commerce nexus. (2) S48(b) gives the video offenses (creation/sale/marketing/distribution, S48(a)(2)-(3)) extraterritorial reach: conduct occurring entirely outside the US is itself a federal violation if the person intends or has reason to know the crush video will be transported into the US, or if it actually is - relevant given documented cases of crush-video production originating outside the US and marketed to US-based buyers. Both points verified directly against the current statutory text (law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/48) on 2026-09-21.

RESOLVED 2026-09-21: the NSW general-criminal-law penalty unit is confirmed at a fixed AUD 110 (s.17, Crimes (Sentencing Procedure) Act 1999, unchanged since 1999 - distinct from the separately-indexed WHS penalty unit, which does not apply here) - AUD conversions above and in penalty_fine_max_local_currency are now populated on that basis.

aggravating_factors: Corporate/body-corporate tier: fine up to NZD 500,000. [SNIPPET-LEVEL, current figures NOT independently verified against primary text this round - see notes for the verified-but-superseded 2007 baseline.]
notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (volunteer fact-checker caught this, batch 3): this row's category_plain previously described 'wilful OR reckless ill-treatment' as if both shared this one penalty figure. They do not - s.28 (wilful ill-treatment, recorded in THIS row) and s.28A (reckless ill-treatment, a genuinely lower-penalty offence) are now split into separate rows; see NZ-AWA1999-P3 for the reckless tier (3yr/NZD75,000 individual, NZD350,000 corporate). UPGRADED 2026-09-15: a real primary-source PDF was recovered (Parliamentary Counsel Office reprint, 'as at 2007-09-03', hosted by University of Auckland's Liggins Institute) after ~10 prior fetch attempts against legislation.govt.nz/nzlii.org all failed - confirmed this round to be a Cloudflare JS-challenge wall, not a URL problem. s.2 (VERIFIED, verbatim): 'Animal' = any live member of the animal kingdom that is a mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, or fish (bony or cartilaginous), OR any octopus, squid, crab, lobster, or crayfish (including freshwater crayfish), or any other species declared by Order in Council; includes mammalian foetuses/avian-reptilian pre-hatched young in the last half of gestation and marsupial pouch young; excludes human beings. This names cephalopods AND decapod crustaceans directly in the statute's primary definition (not via delegated regulation, contrast Switzerland) - hence the new animal_scope value. There is NO section 3A - the 2015 sentience recognition was inserted into the Act's LONG TITLE (statement of purpose) by the Animal Welfare Amendment Act (No 2) 2015, not as an operative numbered section - this is a policy-framing statement, not an independently enforceable provision, an important distinction for cross-jurisdictional comparison. PENALTY HISTORY: 2007-verified baseline (this Act as originally enacted): s.28 (wilful ill-treatment causing permanent disability/death/necessary destruction), on indictment - individual up to 3 years/NZD 50,000, body corporate up to NZD 250,000. This was raised to the current 5-year/NZD 100,000 figure (recorded in this row) via a later amendment; a new s.28A 'Reckless ill-treatment of animals' was inserted 2010-07-07 by the Animal Welfare Amendment Act 2010 (NOT 2015 as this database's prior placeholder speculated) mirroring s.28's threshold. The current dollar figures rest on snippet-level secondary-source corroboration, not a primary-text refetch of the current consolidated version - flag accordingly. No dedicated filming/distribution offence exists in this Act; cruelty content depicting animals MAY fall under the separate Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993's general 'objectionable material' regime (trading up to 14yr, possession up to 10yr/NZD 50,000) - but no confirmed instance of this being applied to an animal-cruelty case was found; this is inference from statutory scope, not a confirmed application, and is not modeled as its own provision row.

aggravating_factors: Personal consumption at a food establishment (Art.16): fine 2-10x assessed value of a non-whitelisted animal, 5-30x if a nationally protected species. Unlicensed commercial production/sale (Art.17-18): flat CNY150,000-200,000 or 20-30x value for protected species. Advertising/menu display of prohibited-animal dishes (Art.19-20): forced removal plus CNY10,000-50,000 fine. penalty_administrative_only=TRUE and no single flat/max figure recorded in the base fields because this instrument sets several distinct violation-type tiers rather than one ceiling - see this field for the full structure.
notes: Art.3 sets a POSITIVE WHITELIST of animals that may be eaten (pigs, cattle, sheep, donkeys, rabbits, chickens, ducks, geese, pigeons, quail listed in the national Livestock and Poultry Genetic Resources Catalogue, plus other catalogue-listed poultry/livestock, plus aquatic animals not otherwise prohibited by law) - anything NOT on this list is prohibited. Cats and dogs are absent from the catalogue, hence prohibited BY OMISSION - the characters 猫 (cat) and 狗 (dog) do not appear anywhere in the 26-article operative text, despite widely-circulated media framing (e.g. "深圳通过条例禁止食用猫狗") describing this as an explicit cat/dog eating ban. Verified directly by searching the fetched raw text for both characters (zero matches) across two independent official mirrors. The Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee's own Legislative Affairs Commission publicly confirmed (2020-04-03 briefing, reported by thepaper.cn and others - snippet-tier as reported speech, not a fetched transcript) that excluding pets via the whitelist mechanism, rather than naming them, was the deliberate legislative approach, citing this as consistent with practice in Hong Kong and Taiwan. This is exactly the kind of widely-misreported legal detail this database exists to correct.

aggravating_factors: Art.14 (personal consumption in restaurants/canteens): non-protected prohibited animals (the tier cats/dogs fall into) -> fine 2-10x assessed value; nationally protected species -> 5-30x. Art.15 (unlicensed commercial production/sale): non-protected prohibited animals -> flat CNY100,000-150,000 (value <CNY10,000) or 15-20x value (value >=CNY10,000); protected species -> CNY150,000-200,000 flat or 20-30x. Xinhua's widely-cited "up to 20x fine" headline (April 2020) refers to the Art.15 commercial-sale ceiling, not the Art.14 personal-consumption ceiling (2-10x) - these are easily conflated in short-form reporting but govern different conduct.
notes: Same whitelist mechanism and structure as Shenzhen (CN-SZ-WILDBAN-P1), functionally identical Art.3 wording. Cats and dogs do not appear anywhere in the 23-article text, confirmed by direct search of the fetched raw text (zero matches). Zhuhai's own Director of the Legislative Affairs Committee (市人大常委会法制工作委员会主任 雍灵) stated unprompted in a 2020-04-14 press briefing (snippet-tier, reported speech) that the Regulation "does not explicitly stipulate" a cat/dog ban and that exclusion instead follows from cats/dogs not being listed in the national livestock catalogue and being unable to obtain quarantine certification - an official, independent corroboration of the whitelist-not-naming mechanism found in the text itself.

Art.17(9) (verbatim): "不得虐待、遗弃所养犬" (must not abuse or abandon dogs kept) - abuse and abandonment are bundled in one clause, not textually separable, hence one provisions row rather than splitting abandonment out (consistent with this database's general practice of not force-splitting a jurisdiction's own bundled clause). ENFORCEMENT GAP, verified by checking every cross-reference in the penalty articles (Arts.28-33): none of them reference Art.17(9) - only Art.17 items (1)-(5) (public-place entry, public transport, elevators, leashing) plus Art.8 and Art.21(3) carry any penalty. This is a real, citable finding: Beijing's anti-abuse/anti-abandonment duty exists in the text with zero attached administrative penalty. penalty_administrative_only left FALSE (not TRUE) deliberately - there is no penalty of ANY kind, administrative or otherwise, not merely an administrative-only one; all penalty fields are blank accordingly, not assumed zero. WATCH ITEM: a pending revision (2nd reading passed 2026-07-29, not yet enacted - see legal_instruments notes) would add 5-year/lifetime ownership bans for exactly this conduct, which would close this gap if and when it passes.

Art.21 (verbatim): "...不得虐待饲养的犬只。" (...must not abuse the dog(s) kept.) ENFORCEMENT GAP, verified by reading the entire 法律责任 (Legal Responsibility) chapter (Arts.41-56) and checking every cross-reference: no article references Art.21 at all - the abuse duty carries zero attached penalty, the same pattern found in Beijing's ordinance (CN-BJ-DOG-P1). Contrast this row with CN-SH-DOG-P2 (the separate abandonment clause, Art.27, which DOES carry a real penalty) - the same instrument treats textually-separate abuse and abandonment very differently in practice. This was confirmed via direct page-by-page reading of the official PDF, not an AI-tool-summarized extraction, and is the highest-confidence fetch in this research round.

Art.27, second paragraph (verbatim): "养犬人不得遗弃饲养的犬只。" (Owners must not abandon dogs kept.) Art.47 attaches a real penalty: fine CNY500-2,000, dog-keeping license revocation, dog confiscation, and a 5-year ban on re-registering to keep a dog. penalty_fine_max_local_currency records the top of the CNY500-2,000 range. This is the sharper of the two Shanghai findings: the same ordinance explicitly bans BOTH abuse (CN-SH-DOG-P1) and abandonment, but only abandonment is actually punished.

Art.23 (verbatim): "...不得虐待或者遗弃犬只。" (...must not abuse or abandon dogs.) Art.50 (verbatim, abuse clause): "违反本条例第二十三条规定，虐待犬只的，可以由公安机关没收犬只，吊销《养犬登记证》，收回犬牌。" - abuse gets confiscation of the dog plus revocation of the registration certificate/tag, but NO separate monetary fine is specified for abuse itself (contrast CN-GZ-DOG-P2, the abandonment clause under the same Art.23/50, which DOES carry an explicit fine). Unlike Beijing and Shanghai, Guangzhou's abuse clause is not toothless - confiscation plus registration revocation is a real, if non-monetary, consequence. penalty_fine_max_local_currency left blank because no fine amount is specified for this specific violation type.

Art.50 (verbatim, abandonment clause): "违反本条例第二十三条规定，遗弃犬只的，由公安机关责令领回犬只或者将犬只送到犬只留验场所；拒不领回犬只或者拒不将犬只送到犬只留验场所的，处每只犬一千元以上二千元以下罚款。" - a mandatory reclaim order (or surrender to a holding facility) in the first instance; the CNY1,000-2,000 fine (recorded here at its CNY2,000 ceiling) only applies to REFUSAL to comply with that order, not to the act of abandonment itself directly. A 2019 draft revision would have raised this to CNY2,000/CNY5,000 (individual/unit) but never passed; a further 2025 revision effort ran public consultation (2025-09-05 to 2025-10-06, 295 comments) but has not passed as of 2026-09-15 - the figures here remain the current, effective ones.

ENTIRE ROW IS SNIPPET-TIER - see CN-CD-DOG instrument notes; no .gov.cn or Sichuan NPC primary text located this round, only mutually consistent state/city-media reprints. Per those sources: a prohibition (reported as Art.28(1)) states "日常饲养中，严禁虐待、遗弃犬只" (abuse and abandonment bundled in one clause, as in Beijing and Guangzhou), with a reported penalty (Art.42(3)): "有虐待或遗弃犬只行为的，责令改正，处五百元以上一千元以下罚款；拒不改正的，可以没收犬只，并吊销养犬登记。" - correction order + fine CNY500-1,000 (recorded here at the CNY1,000 ceiling), escalating to confiscation and registration revocation on refusal to correct, plus a reported 5-year reregistration ban (Art.44) mirroring Shanghai's mechanism. If accurate, this would be the strongest of the five cities' abuse clauses on paper (a real fine, unlike Beijing/Shanghai's toothless clauses) - but this rests entirely on secondary reporting of a regulation that took effect only weeks before this research (2026-08-01) and should be re-verified against a primary source before being trusted at face value.

Art.27 (verbatim): "从事实验动物工作的人员对实验动物必须爱护，不得戏弄或虐待。" (Personnel engaged in laboratory-animal work must care for laboratory animals and must not toy with or abuse them.) ENFORCEMENT IS GENERIC, NOT ABUSE-SPECIFIC, verified by reading the entire "奖励与处罚" (Rewards and Penalties) chapter: Art.29 (institutions) imposes warning/deadline-to-correct/forced-closure for violating ANY provision of the Regulation - quality-control failures and licensing lapses get the identical penalty as an Art.27 abuse violation, there is no distinct heavier consequence for abuse specifically. Art.30 (individual staff) is even weaker: the consequence is an internal disciplinary action decided by the person's OWN EMPLOYER, not any external government sanction - an individual researcher who abuses a laboratory animal is, under this statute, answerable only to their own institution's internal process. A non-binding companion guidance document (国科发财字〔2006〕398号, 2006, Ministry of Science and Technology) elaborates "5 freedoms"-style welfare language this Regulation lacks in detail, but carries no independent legal force. Original 1988 enactment revised 2011/2013/2017; effective_date recorded here is the current (2017) revision's effective date.

Art.2 (verbatim): comprehensively prohibits eating state-protected terrestrial wildlife of "important ecological, scientific, or social value" and other terrestrial wildlife, INCLUDING artificially-bred and artificially-raised terrestrial wildlife - broader than CN-WPL-P1 (which only reaches captive-bred wildlife abuse, not consumption of it). Art.3 draws the wildlife/livestock boundary via the 畜禽遗传资源目录 (Livestock and Poultry Genetic Resources Catalogue) - the identical mechanism every municipal whitelist ordinance in this database (Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Guangzhou, Beijing) later cites verbatim. No fine/penalty amount is set by this Decision itself - Art.1 instead directs that violations "在现行法律规定基础上加重处罚" (be penalized more heavily than under EXISTING law), i.e. it raises the penalty ceiling of WPL/Criminal Law Art.341 rather than creating an independent penalty schedule; penalty fields left blank accordingly rather than fabricated. penalty_administrative_only=FALSE because the Decision explicitly contemplates criminal-law-level enforcement (via Criminal Law Art.341, CN-CL341 in this database) for qualifying violations, not administrative sanctions only. Art.4 requires strict approval/quarantine for non-food wildlife uses including "展示" (display) - an early textual signal, independent of CN-ZOOSTD, that national policy treats zoo/display use as distinct from ordinary captive breeding.

Art.2 (verbatim): "列入畜禽遗传资源目录的动物，属于家禽家畜，按照《中华人民共和国畜牧法》的规定执行。" - the identical catalogue-whitelist mechanism as CN-SZ-WILDBAN-P1/CN-ZH-WILDBAN-P1. Cats and dogs confirmed absent from the 29-article operative text by direct search (zero matches for 猫/狗) - same omission-not-naming pattern. Art.1 explicitly cites CN-NPCDECISION-2020 by name as enabling authority. Specific penalty figures for this ordinance were not verbatim-quoted in this research round's report - penalty_administrative_only set TRUE consistent with the parallel Shenzhen/Zhuhai instruments' administrative-fine structure, but specific amounts left blank pending a future round confirming the exact penalty article text.

Arts.25-26 (consumption ban, folded into a comprehensive 46-article wildlife-protection rewrite rather than a standalone ordinance like Shenzhen/Zhuhai/Guangzhou). Art.25 uses the identical catalogue carve-out: "对列入名录的野生动物，人工繁育技术成熟稳定，依法列入畜禽遗传资源目录的，属于家禽家畜，依照有关畜牧法律法规的规定执行。" Art.26 (the ban itself) names no specific species. Confirmed zero mentions of 猫/狗 in the full 46-article text. Art.1 explicitly cites CN-NPCDECISION-2020 as enabling authority. This instrument's final article repeals Beijing's 1989 wildlife-protection implementing measures (as amended 1997/2018). Specific penalty figures for Arts.25-26 themselves were not verbatim-quoted in this round's report (see CN-BJ-WILDLIFE-P2 for a DIFFERENT, confirmed-verbatim penalty elsewhere in this same instrument) - penalty_administrative_only set TRUE by analogy to the parallel municipal instruments, specific amount left blank pending confirmation.

Art.24(8) (verbatim): "不得虐待野生动物" (must not abuse wildlife), a duty on captive-breeding operations, backed by a REAL penalty: Art.39 fines violation of Art.24 CNY20,000-100,000 (recorded here at the CNY100,000 ceiling). This covers the SAME population as CN-WPL-P1 (captive-bred wildlife) but is a Beijing-local supplementary penalty on top of the national WPL Art.26 administrative-multiplier structure - unlike the toothless dog-abuse clauses documented for Beijing's own dog-keeping ordinance (CN-BJ-DOG-P1), this wildlife-abuse duty in the SAME city's wildlife ordinance is genuinely enforced with a fixed fine. A related but distinct clause, Art.15(4) ("不得虐待收容救护的野生动物" - must not abuse wildlife in rescue/rehabilitation custody), is backed by a separate CNY10,000-50,000 fine (Art.36) - not separately modeled as its own row since it protects a different population (rescued wildlife, not captive-BRED wildlife) but recorded here for completeness.

CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (audit caught this): moved a scope/prohibited-conduct description out of aggravating_factors, where it had been wrongly placed - this row has no penalty of any kind (it's a voluntary standard, see below), so there is nothing to aggravate. Art.2.0.13 (verbatim): zoos shall not (1) use wildlife for performances, (2) feed live prey animals within visitors' sightlines, or (3) use wildlife as props for commercial activities - a genuine performance/exploitation ban, not merely a duty-of-care standard. Art.1.0.1 (verbatim) states protecting "动物福利" (animal welfare) as an explicit purpose of the standard - the first instance in this database of a Chinese instrument naming welfare as a purpose in its own text. Art.2.0.5(2) (verbatim): "应保障动物福利，为动物提供适宜的饲养场所、饲料、医疗保健" (must protect animal welfare, providing suitable housing, feed, and medical/health care). Further chapters (verified by direct reading, not restated verbatim here) cover feed-quality standards (Ch.4), behavioral-enrichment requirements aimed at reducing abnormal behavior (Ch.5, Art.5.1.2), veterinary staffing/anesthesia-safety protocols (Ch.6), and welfare-framed transport standards (Ch.7.4, e.g. extreme-weather avoidance, oxygen supply for air transport). CRITICAL CAVEAT, penalty_administrative_only deliberately set FALSE (not TRUE): this is a "推荐性" (voluntary) industry standard, not mandatory law - there is NO independent penalty mechanism for non-compliance of any kind, administrative or otherwise, distinguishing it from every other FALSE-penalty row in this database, which mostly represent an enforcement gap in an otherwise-binding law rather than a non-binding standard by design. A 2013 People's Daily (人民网) article reports on-record acknowledgment that a predecessor MOHURD document making the same performance-ban demand (2010, 建城〔2010〕172号) "became a dead letter" because it was administrative guidance, not law - the same practical-enforcement risk should be assumed here absent evidence otherwise. Distinguish from 《城市动物园管理规定》(1994 Order No.37, genuinely legally-binding) which DOES apply to zoos but was confirmed, by full direct reading, to contain zero welfare content of its own - see CN-ZOOSTD instrument notes.

aggravating_factors: Personal consumption: confiscation plus fine 2-10x product value. Commercial production/sale: CNY100,000-150,000 (value <CNY10,000) or 15-30x value (value >=CNY10,000). Platform operators facilitating illegal trade: CNY100,000-200,000. Coded animal_scope=protected_wildlife_species_only as the closest existing fit, though per a snippet-tier summary the actual scope is somewhat broader (also covers "other terrestrial wild animals naturally growing and reproducing in wild environments," not strictly limited to a formally protected list) - flagged rather than force-fitting a new controlled value on snippet-tier, paraphrased (not verbatim) content.
notes: ENTIRE ROW IS SNIPPET-TIER - see CN-TJ-WILDBAN instrument notes. Mandates a to-be-published named catalogue of prohibited wildlife rather than the livestock-whitelist-by-omission mechanism used by every later instrument in this database (CN-NPCDECISION-2020, CN-SZ-WILDBAN, CN-ZH-WILDBAN, CN-GZ-WILDBAN, CN-BJ-WILDLIFE) - the earliest-dated wildlife-consumption instrument in this database (2020-02-14), predating the national Decision by ten days.

Art.1 (near-verbatim): prohibits consuming (1) nationally protected wildlife, (2) provincially protected wildlife, (3) other terrestrial wildlife of "important ecological, scientific, or social value" designated by the State Council's wildlife authority, and other wild-growing/reproducing terrestrial wildlife - direct enumerated-category coverage with NO livestock-catalogue whitelist carve-out (that mechanism arrived six days later with CN-NPCDECISION-2020). Coded animal_scope=protected_wildlife_species_only as the closest existing fit, though the actual textual scope extends somewhat beyond formally protected species - same caveat as CN-TJ-WILDBAN-P1. Art.10: violations face administrative penalties escalating to public-security or criminal sanctions depending on conduct (illegal consumption; producing/selling prohibited-species food; hunting/trading for food; platform facilitation; using prohibited species in advertising) - penalty_administrative_only set FALSE since criminal-level sanction is explicitly contemplated, not merely administrative. Art.13: administrative penalties additionally trigger social-credit-system reporting and coordinated economic sanctions - an enforcement mechanism not seen elsewhere in this database, not modeled as a separate ancillary_orders token since none of the existing controlled values fit "credit-system reporting."

Subd.(a) (malicious/intentional maiming, mutilation, torture, or killing) and subd.(c) (same conduct against an enumerated protected/endangered species list, cross-referencing Fish and Game Code chapters) - both punishable per subd.(d) as EITHER a felony (imprisonment per Penal Code sec.1170(h): 16 months, 2, or 3 years, in COUNTY jail not state prison, a post-2011-Realignment structural feature) OR a misdemeanor (up to 1 year county jail), a prosecutorial/judicial "wobbler" choice with NO prior-conviction gate - felony treatment is available on a genuine first offence. Subd.(e)'s species enumeration narrows ONLY subd.(c)'s enhanced tier, not this row's general (a) coverage, which applies to undefined "a living animal." Widely-cited claim "California has the strongest animal cruelty law in the US" is TRUE on this specific structural dimension (felony-eligible on a genuine first offence, reaching neglect too via US-CA-PC597-P2) but does NOT hold as a general ranking claim - ALDF's 2025 holistic ~20-category ranking places Oregon #1 for the third consecutive year, with California not in the top 5. CHECKED 2026-09-17 (an independent audit flagged the 2024-01-01 effective_date as possibly borrowed from AM1's unrelated counseling-order change): confirmed directly against leginfo.legislature.ca.gov's own official page for this section - AB 829 (Stats.2023, Ch.546, Sec.2, effective 2024-01-01) IS genuinely this section's most recent amendment of any kind, so 2024-01-01 is the legitimate date this section's current text was last codified, even though the wobbler penalty structure itself carried over unchanged from an earlier version. Not a misattribution.

Subd.(b): overdriving/overloading/overworking, depriving of sustenance/water/shelter, failing to provide proper food/drink/shelter/weather protection, or otherwise abusing an animal in one's charge/custody. Punishable under the SAME subd.(d) felony-or-misdemeanor wobbler as US-CA-PC597-P1 (general cruelty) - a genuinely notable finding: California extends first-offence felony eligibility to PASSIVE neglect/failure-to-provide-care conduct, not merely intentional active cruelty, with no prior-conviction gate anywhere in the text. This is broader than the popular "felony on first offense" framing of California law usually conveys.

aggravating_factors: Escalates to a SECOND-degree felony (2-20 years, i.e. up to 240 months) with one prior qualifying conviction under subd.(b)(1)/(2)/(7)/(8) or sec.42.09 - the highest criminal exposure of any jurisdiction in this database. penalty_criminal_max_months records the first-offence ceiling (120=10yr, third-degree felony) for cross-jurisdiction comparability; the repeat-offence ceiling is recorded here rather than in the base field. "Pancho's Law" (H.B. 285, effective 2025-09-01) added a criminal-negligence mens rea to this subsection, alongside the pre-existing intentional/knowing/reckless standard, with a defense for veterinarians/veterinary staff acting within their professional duties.
notes: Subd.(b)(1)/(2): torture, cruel killing, or killing/poisoning/serious injury without owner consent - a THIRD-degree felony on a genuine first offence (2-10 years state prison, not county jail as in California), via general Penal Code felony-punishment ranges (secs.12.33-12.35, snippet-tier general-knowledge cross-check, not independently re-verified from the code sections themselves this round). "Animal" is defined (subd.(a)(2)) as a domesticated living creature (including stray/feral cats and dogs) or a previously-captured wild creature - explicitly EXCLUDING an uncaptured wild creature and a livestock animal (livestock covered separately, see US-TX-PC4209-P1). effective_date recorded as 2007 (year of subd.(b)(1)/(2)'s enactment via H.B. 2328) - exact day/month not confirmed, treated as 2007-01-01 as a best-available placeholder rather than left entirely blank, since the addition is a whole-provision creation rather than an amendment to a pre-existing effective date.

aggravating_factors: Subd.(b)(3)/(4)/(5)/(6)/(9) (unreasonable failure to provide food/water/care/shelter, unreasonable abandonment, cruel transport/confinement, causing bodily injury without consent, serious overwork) is a Class A misdemeanor on a first offence (Texas's standard Class A misdemeanor ceiling is 1 year/12 months county jail under general Penal Code provisions - not independently re-verified from sec.12.21 itself this round, recorded here as established general-law background rather than a fresh primary-source finding), escalating to a STATE JAIL FELONY (180 days-2 years, recorded here at the 24-month ceiling) after TWO prior convictions under sec.42.092 (this section) or sec.42.09, or one conviction under each.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (volunteer fact-checker caught this, batch 8): effective_date was recorded as a hedged '2007-01-01' placeholder; the exact date is confirmed and not a hedge-worthy detail - this provision was added by Acts 2007, 80th Legislature, Regular Session, Chapter 886 (H.B. 2328), Section 2, effective 2007-09-01 (Texas's standard September 1 commencement for that session's regular-session enactments). penalty_criminal_max_months records the ESCALATED (2-prior) state-jail-felony ceiling rather than the first-offence Class A misdemeanor ceiling (12 months) - flagged here explicitly since this differs from the first-offence-ceiling convention used for US-TX-PC42092-P1, because the Class A misdemeanor's exact statutory month-cap was not independently re-verified from primary text this round (general TX law background only) while the escalated state-jail-felony range WAS explicitly confirmed (snippet-tier, three mutually consistent sources). Separately, a 2025 amendment (H.B. 285, 'Pancho's Law', effective 2025-09-01) added a criminal-negligence mental state and a veterinarian defense to sec.42.092 as a whole - already tracked as US-TX-PC42092-AM1 in amendments.csv; noted here per the same volunteer's request that this row's own text point to it rather than leaving the 2025 update unexplained.

aggravating_factors: Structurally mirrors US-TX-PC42092-P1's tiering (this row records the same 120-month/10-year first-offence ceiling) and cross-references sec.42.092 for recidivism escalation in both directions (subd.(c)) - a prior conviction under either statute counts toward the other's repeat-offence tier.
notes: "Livestock animal" (sec.42.09(b)(5)) = cattle/sheep/swine/goats/ratites/poultry raised for consumption, horses/ponies/mules/donkeys/hinnies, and other native/nonnative hoofstock or fowl raised under agricultural practice. Act-list (torture; failure to provide food/water/care; abandonment; cruel-and-unusual transport/confinement; poisoning non-cattle/horse/sheep/swine/goat livestock without consent; fighting; lure use; horse-tripping; overwork) was NOT itself broken into the same active/passive two-way split as sec.42.092 in the sources consulted this round - recorded as one row pending a future round that might separately verify a neglect-specific sub-tier if one exists. Carries a broad exemption for "animal husbandry or agriculture practice involving livestock animals" that is otherwise generally accepted.

aggravating_factors: Repeat (2nd+) major offence: fine ceiling doubles to CAD260,000 (individual) - but the maximum imprisonment term does NOT increase for repeat offenders, only the fine. Corporation tier: CAD500,000 (1st)/CAD1,000,000 (2nd+). A CAD25,000 statutory MINIMUM fine applies where the offence caused the animal's death/required euthanasia, or for fighting/harming-a-law-enforcement-animal. Directors/officers who authorize or participate in a corporate offence are personally liable at the INDIVIDUAL penalty tier (s.49(8)), regardless of whether the corporation itself is prosecuted.
notes: s.15(1): "No person shall cause an animal to be in distress" - a "major" offence per s.49(2)'s tiering. "Distress" (s.1(1)) = in need of proper care/water/food/shelter; injured/sick/in pain/suffering; or abused/subject to undue physical or psychological hardship, privation, or neglect - this row is coded general_cruelty as the closest existing controlled value, though the Act's own operative vocabulary is "distress," never "cruelty" (see instrument notes). penalty_administrative_only=FALSE per this project's established convention for a genuinely quasi-criminal (not administrative-civil, not Criminal-Code) Provincial Offences Act prosecution with real imprisonment available. Agricultural exemption (s.15(4)/(5)): does not apply to "reasonable and generally accepted practices of agricultural animal care, management or husbandry" absent a specific contrary standard-of-care regulation, nor to permitted wildlife activity, nor to veterinary care.

aggravating_factors: Same major-offence penalty structure and repeat-offence doubling as CA-ON-PAWS-P1 (see that row).
notes: s.15(2): "No owner or custodian of an animal shall permit the animal to be in distress" - the owner/custodian duty-of-care counterpart to s.15(1)'s general prohibition, also a "major" offence under s.49(2). Same agricultural/wildlife/veterinary exemptions as CA-ON-PAWS-P1 apply.

aggravating_factors: Art.70: fine minimums/maximums DOUBLE on a first repeat offence, TRIPLE on any subsequent repeat. Imprisonment exists ONLY as this recidivist enhancement, and only for Art.68/69-tier offences: up to 6 months (1st repeat) or 12 months (further repeat) for an Art.68 offence (this row). Art.75 requires the judge to weigh explicit statutory aggravating factors (severity, number of animals, duration, foreseeability, intentionality vs. recklessness vs. negligence, financial benefit, financial capacity to have prevented harm) when setting the fine within its tier. Art.76: a prohibition on owning/having custody of animals may be imposed PERPETUALLY for an individual (or a corporation they control). Art.71: a corporate officer/director who personally commits a violation is punished at the HIGHER corporate fine tier, not the lower individual tier - a distinctive inversion not seen elsewhere in this database. Art.77: prosecutions may be brought in municipal court by the local municipality, which keeps the resulting fines.
notes: Art.6 (verbatim): "Nul ne peut, par son acte ou son omission, faire en sorte qu'un animal soit en détresse" (No person may, by act or omission, cause an animal to be in distress) - "détresse" defined by three sub-clauses (treatment causing death/serious injury if not immediately modified; treatment causing acute pain; conditions causing excessive anxiety/suffering). Penalty per Art.68 (the tier covering Art.6 among others): CAD2,500-62,500 (individual)/CAD5,000-125,000 (other) - GENUINELY ZERO months' imprisonment available for a FIRST offence at any severity, confirmed by reading the full penal chapter (Arts.65-77); this is a verified, deliberate finding, not a data-entry gap - flag prominently rather than assuming an omission. Art.7 exempts agriculture, veterinary medicine, teaching, and scientific research "practiced according to generally recognized rules" from Arts.5-6 entirely, explicitly including slaughter/euthanasia and agricultural-exhibition use.

aggravating_factors: Same Art.68 penalty tier, Art.70 doubling/tripling recidivist mechanism, and Art.75-77 provisions as CA-QC-BWSA-P1 (see that row).
notes: Art.5 (verbatim): "Le propriétaire ou la personne ayant la garde d'un animal doit s'assurer que le bien-être ou la sécurité de l'animal n'est pas compromis" (The owner or person having custody of an animal must ensure the animal's welfare or safety is not compromised), presumed compromised when the animal does not receive care suited to its biological needs - followed by seven enumerated care standards (water/food; clean/spacious/well-lit housing; exercise; weather protection; transport; veterinary care; no abuse/mistreatment affecting health). "Animal" (BWSA Art.1) is a CLOSED ENUMERATED LIST (cat, dog, rabbit, cattle, horse, pig, sheep, goat, chicken, and hybrids, plus fur-farm mink/fox, plus regulation-designated others) - materially NARROWER than the "animals are sentient beings" headline (CA-QC-CCQ8981) implies; wild companion animals are explicitly carved out to a separate wildlife-conservation statute.

s.23.2(1) (verbatim): "A person must not cause an animal to be in distress." "Distress" (s.1(2)) covers deprivation of food/water/shelter/care/veterinary treatment, unsanitary conditions, exposure to excessive heat/cold, injury/sickness/pain/suffering, or abuse/neglect. GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE FINDING: s.24.1 sets a SINGLE FLAT penalty ($75,000/24 months) applying UNIFORMLY to every offence under the Act - active distress-causing (this row), owner/custodian neglect (CA-BC-PCAA-P2), unsafe transport, service-animal harm, animal fighting, AND obstruction of an enforcement officer all share the identical ceiling, with no severity tiering whatsoever (unlike California/Texas/Ontario/Quebec, all of which grade penalties by conduct severity). CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (independent audit caught this): effective_date was wrongly recorded as 2011-01-01 with a note claiming the exact day/month wasn't confirmed - but amendments.csv's CA-BC-PCAA-AM1 row already established, from direct reading of the amending Act's own text, that it "comes into force on Royal Assent" (s.11), which was 2011-06-02. That date is used here now; the prior note's claim of non-confirmation was simply wrong given information already in this dataset. The ownership-prohibition order (s.24(3)) has no maximum duration stated in the text - unlike Quebec's Art.76, which explicitly permits a perpetual order, BC's text is silent on whether an unstated-duration order could run for life; flagged as an unresolved textual ambiguity, not assumed either way. Limitation period is 3 years (extended from a pre-2011 6-month period, snippet-tier for the "before" figure).

s.9.1 (Part 2.1, "Standards of care"): places an owner/custodian duty not to cause or permit an animal to be in distress, tied to the same s.1(2) distress definition as CA-BC-PCAA-P1. Same flat $75,000/24-month penalty ceiling applies (s.24.1) - see that row for the no-severity-tiering finding, which applies identically here. This Part also establishes an "operator"/"regulated activity" concept (ss.9.2-9.3, unsafe transport) added by the same 2011 reform. CORRECTED 2026-09-17: effective_date fixed to 2011-06-02 (Royal Assent, confirmed in amendments.csv CA-BC-PCAA-AM1) - see CA-BC-PCAA-P1's note for the same correction.

s.2 prohibits causing an animal to be in distress (s.1(2) definition, near-identical language to BC and Ontario). CURRENTLY IN FORCE penalty, s.12(1) (verbatim, in full): "A person who contravenes this Act or the regulations is guilty of an offence and liable to a fine of not more than $20,000." GENUINELY VERIFIED ZERO: there is NO imprisonment available for ANY Animal Protection Act offence today, at any severity - more extreme than Quebec's "no imprisonment on a first offence" pattern, since Alberta currently has no imprisonment provision at all, first offence or otherwise. penalty_criminal_max_months=0 is a deliberate, verified finding, not a data-entry gap. The only other consequence is a discretionary ownership-prohibition order (s.12(2)), no maximum duration stated. PENDING (NOT YET IN FORCE): Bill 22 (assented 2026-05-14, not proclaimed as of 2026-09-16) would replace this with a $250,000 fine and up to 12 months' imprisonment, plus per-animal/per-day multiplication, a disgorgement-style order, and a much richer prohibition-order regime - see CA-AB-APA instrument notes. Coded to CURRENT law only, per this project's standing practice; re-check for proclamation before the next data refresh.

s.2/s.2.1 owner/custodian duty-of-care counterpart to CA-AB-APA-P1's general distress prohibition, sharing the identical currently-in-force penalty structure (s.12(1): $20,000 fine, no imprisonment at any severity) and the same pending Bill 22 upgrade - see CA-AB-APA-P1 and instrument notes for the full pending-law detail, not repeated here.

Art.29(3) (verbatim): "养犬人不得有下列行为：...（三）虐待、遗弃犬只" (Dog keepers must not: ...(3) abuse or abandon dogs) - abuse and abandonment bundled in one clause, same pattern as Beijing (CN-BJ-DOG-P1) and Chengdu (CN-CD-DOG-P1), not split like Shanghai/Guangzhou. UNLIKE Beijing and Shanghai's toothless version of this same bundled clause, Zibo's Art.46(9) attaches a REAL, cross-referenced penalty (verbatim): "虐待、遗弃犬只的，责令改正，对个人处每只二百元以上五百元以下罚款，对单位处每只一千元罚款。" - a correction order plus a fine of CNY200-500 per dog for individuals (recorded here at the CNY500 ceiling) or a flat CNY1,000 per dog for units/entities (not separately fielded - this schema has no individual-vs-unit split, see this note for the unit figure). Confirmed via two independently fetched sources giving identical verbatim text (SRC-CN-18) - joins Guangzhou (confiscation, no fine) and Chengdu (snippet-tier, unverified primary text) as the cities in this database where the abuse/abandonment duty is not purely symbolic, and is the strongest VERIFIED-tier case of a working penalty among the six Chinese cities examined so far.

aggravating_factors: Corporate/body-corporate tier: fine up to NZD350,000.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (audit caught this): moved a comparative/mitigating note out of aggravating_factors, where it had been wrongly placed (that field is for circumstances that escalate a penalty, not a reason this row's own penalty is lower than a different row's). For clarity: this tier is deliberately LOWER than s.28's wilful-ill-treatment tier (NZ-AWA1999-P1: 5yr/NZD100,000 individual, NZD500,000 corporate) - recklessness is a less culpable mental state than wilfulness under this Act's own structure. NEW ROW 2026-09-18, split out from NZ-AWA1999-P1 after a volunteer fact-checker (batch 3) caught that the prior single row wrongly presented wilful and reckless ill-treatment as sharing one penalty. s.28A 'Reckless ill-treatment of animals', inserted 2010-07-07 by the Animal Welfare Amendment Act 2010 (same insertion date already on record for NZ-AWA1999-P1). Covers ill-treatment causing the same categories of serious harm as s.28 (permanent disability, death, necessary destruction) but where the person's state of mind was reckless rather than wilful - e.g. leaving an animal in circumstances likely to cause serious harm without intending that harm, as opposed to deliberately causing it. Direct fetch of legislation.govt.nz and an AustLII mirror both returned HTTP 403 (the same Cloudflare wall already documented elsewhere in this jurisdiction's rows) - this is a WebSearch-synthesized figure, snippet tier, not independently read from primary text.
